title.zh: 卷六十八 閩世家第八: 王審知
title.raw: 卷六十八 閩世家第八: 王審知 Volume 68: Hereditary House of Min

sentences.zh: 王審知，字信通，光州固始人也。

translations.literal: Wang Shenzhi, styled Xintong, was a native of Gushi in Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shenzhi, whose style name was Xintong, came from Gushi in Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父恁，世為農。

translations.literal: His father Ren had been farmers for generations.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ren's family had farmed for generations.

sentences.zh: 兄潮，為縣史。

translations.literal: His elder brother Chao served as a county clerk.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Chao held the post of county clerk.

sentences.zh: 唐末群盜起，壽州人王緒攻陷固始，緒聞潮兄弟材勇，召置軍中，以潮為軍校。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tang, bandits rose everywhere; Wang Xu of Shou Prefecture captured Gushi; Xu heard that the Chao brothers were talented and brave, summoned them into his army, and made Chao a military officer.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang dynasty was collapsing and rebels swarmed the realm, a man from Shou Prefecture named Wang Xu seized Gushi. Hearing of the Chao brothers' courage and ability, Xu enrolled them in his forces and appointed Chao a company commander.

sentences.zh: 是時，蔡州秦宗權方募士以益兵，乃以緒為光州刺史，召其兵會擊黃巢。

translations.literal: At that time Qin Zongquan of Cai Prefecture was recruiting men to augment his troops; he therefore appointed Xu governor of Guang Prefecture and summoned his army to join in attacking Huang Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zongquan of Cai Prefecture was then recruiting soldiers to swell his ranks. He named Xu governor of Guang Prefecture and called on his troops to march with him against Huang Chao.

sentences.zh: 緒遲留不行，宗權發兵攻緒。

translations.literal: Xu delayed and would not advance; Zongquan sent troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu lingered and refused to move, so Zongquan sent an army against him.

sentences.zh: 緒率眾南奔，所至剽掠，自南康入臨汀，陷漳浦，有眾數萬。

translations.literal: Xu led his multitude south in flight, plundering wherever they went; from Nankang they entered Linting, captured Zhangpu, and had a force of several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Xu fled south with his host, looting every district they passed through. They marched from Nankang into Linting, took Zhangpu, and mustered a force of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 緒性猜忌，部將有材能者，多因事殺之，潮頗自懼。

translations.literal: Xu was by nature suspicious; subordinate officers who had ability he often killed on one pretext or another, and Chao grew quite fearful for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was suspicious by temperament and routinely found excuses to kill capable subordinates. Chao began to fear for his life.

sentences.zh: 軍次南安，潮說其前鋒將曰：「吾屬棄墳墓、妻子而為盜者，為緒所脅爾，豈其本心哉！

translations.literal: When the army halted at Nan'an, Chao said to the vanguard commander: "We abandoned graves, wives, and children to become bandits only because Xu coerced us—was that truly our hearts' desire!
translations.idiomatic: When the army encamped at Nan'an, Chao addressed the vanguard commander: "We left our ancestors' graves and our families behind to live as outlaws only because Xu forced us—surely that was never what we wanted!

sentences.zh: 今緒雄猜，將吏之材能者必死，吾屬不自保朝夕，況欲圖成事哉！

translations.literal: Now Xu is fierce and suspicious; officers and clerks with ability are certain to die—we cannot preserve ourselves from morning to night, let alone plan to accomplish great deeds!
translations.idiomatic: Xu is brutal and mistrustful now; any officer with talent is as good as dead. We cannot count on living from one day to the next, much less hope to achieve anything lasting!

sentences.zh: 」前鋒將大悟，與潮相持而泣。

translations.literal: " The vanguard commander was greatly enlightened and, embracing Chao, wept with him.
translations.idiomatic: " The vanguard commander was deeply moved; he and Chao clung to each other and wept.

sentences.zh: 乃選壯士數十人，伏篁竹間，伺緒至，躍出擒之，囚之軍中。

translations.literal: They then selected several dozen stalwart men, hid among bamboo groves, waited until Xu arrived, leaped out and seized him, and imprisoned him in the camp.
translations.idiomatic: They chose several dozen strong men, concealed them in a bamboo thicket, and when Xu arrived sprang out to seize him and hold him prisoner in the camp.

sentences.zh: 緒後自殺。

translations.literal: Xu later killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xu later took his own life.

sentences.zh: 審知為人狀兒雄偉，隆準方口，常乘白馬，軍中號「白馬三郎」。

translations.literal: Shenzhi in person was imposing in stature, with a high nose and square mouth; he often rode a white horse, and in the army they called him "Third Son on the White Horse."
translations.idiomatic: Shenzhi was a man of imposing build, with a prominent nose and square jaw. He habitually rode a white horse, and the troops nicknamed him the Third Son on the White Horse.

sentences.zh: 乾寧四年，潮卒，審知代立。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qianning, Chao died and Shenzhi succeeded him in power.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Qianning era, Chao died and Shenzhi took his place as leader.

sentences.zh: 唐以福州為威武軍，拜審知節度使，累遷同中書門下平章事，封瑯琊王。

translations.literal: The Tang made Fuzhou the Weiwu Army district, appointed Shenzhi military governor, repeatedly promoted him to Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Langya.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang court organized Fuzhou as the Weiwu military circuit and appointed Shenzhi its governor. He rose through successive promotions to Grand Councilor and was enfeoffed as Prince of Langya.

sentences.zh: 唐亡，梁太祖加拜審知中書令，封閩王，升福州為大都督府。

translations.literal: When the Tang perished, the Liang founding emperor further appointed Shenzhi Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed him as King of Min, and elevated Fuzhou to a great metropolitan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tang fell, the Liang founding emperor invested Shenzhi as Director of the Secretariat and King of Min, and raised Fuzhou to the status of a metropolitan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是時，楊行密據有江淮，審知歲遣使泛海，自登、萊朝貢於梁，使者入海，覆溺常十三四。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Xingmi held the Jianghuai region; Shenzhi each year sent envoys by sea from Deng and Lai to present tribute to the Liang; when the envoys entered the ocean, shipwrecks commonly claimed three or four out of ten.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi then controlled the lower Yangtze, so Shenzhi sent annual missions by sea from Deng and Lai to pay tribute to the Liang. Roughly three or four envoys in ten were lost when their ships foundered at sea.

sentences.zh: 審知雖起盜賊，而為人儉約，好禮下士。

translations.literal: Although Shenzhi had risen from banditry, as a man he was frugal and restrained, honored ritual, and treated scholars with deference.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shenzhi had begun as a rebel, in office he lived simply, honored ritual, and treated men of learning with respect.

sentences.zh: 王淡，唐相溥之子；

translations.literal: Wang Dan, son of the Tang chancellor Wang Pu;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan, son of the Tang chancellor Wang Pu;

sentences.zh: 楊沂，唐相涉從弟；

translations.literal: Yang Yi, a younger cousin of the Tang chancellor Yang She;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi, a cousin of the Tang chancellor Yang She;

sentences.zh: 徐寅，唐時知名進士，皆依審知仕宦。

translations.literal: and Xu Yin, a renowned jinshi degree-holder of the Tang—all relied on Shenzhi and entered official service under him.
translations.idiomatic: and Xu Yin, a celebrated Tang jinshi—all took service under Shenzhi.

sentences.zh: 又建學四門，以教閩士之秀者。

translations.literal: He also founded a Four Gates Academy to instruct the finest scholars of Min.
translations.idiomatic: He also established a Four Gates Academy to educate the most promising scholars of Min.

sentences.zh: 招來海中蠻夷商賈。

translations.literal: He attracted barbarian merchants from across the sea.
translations.idiomatic: He drew overseas merchants from the southern seas to trade in his ports.

sentences.zh: 海上黃崎，波濤為陰，一夕風雨雷電震擊，開以為港，閩人以為審知德政所致，號為甘棠港。

translations.literal: At Huangqi on the sea, waves and billows had blocked the passage; in one night wind, rain, thunder, and lightning struck and opened it as a harbor; the people of Min believed this was due to Shenzhi's virtuous government and named it Sweet Pear Harbor.
translations.idiomatic: At Huangqi on the coast, treacherous seas had long blocked the approach. One night a storm of wind, rain, thunder, and lightning tore open a channel that became a harbor. The people of Min credited Shenzhi's benevolent rule and called it Sweet Pear Harbor.

sentences.zh: 審知同光三年卒，年六十四，謚曰忠懿。

translations.literal: Shenzhi died in the third year of Tongguang, aged sixty-four; his posthumous title was Loyal and Cultivated.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzhi died in the third year of Tongguang at the age of sixty-four. He was given the posthumous title Loyal and Cultivated.

sentences.zh: 子延翰立。

translations.literal: His son Yanhan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanhan took the throne.

sentences.zh: 延翰字子逸，審知長子也。

translations.literal: Yanhan, styled Ziyi, was Shenzhi's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhan, whose style name was Ziyi, was Shenzhi's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 同光四年，唐拜延翰節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tongguang the Tang appointed Yanhan military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tongguang the Tang court appointed Yanhan military governor of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 是歲，莊宗遇弒，中國多故，延翰乃取司馬遷《史記》閩越王無諸傳示其將吏曰：「閩，自古王國也，吾今不王，何待之有？

translations.literal: That year Emperor Zhuangzong was assassinated and the central realm was in turmoil; Yanhan then took Sima Qian's Records of the Grand Historian, the biography of Minyue's King Wuzhu, and showed it to his generals and officials, saying: "Min has been a kingdom since antiquity—if I do not become king now, what am I waiting for?
translations.idiomatic: That year Emperor Zhuangzong was murdered and the empire fell into disorder. Yanhan produced from Sima Qian's Records the biography of Wuzhu, king of ancient Minyue, and showed it to his commanders and officials, saying, "Min has been a kingdom since antiquity. If I do not claim kingship now, how long should I wait?

sentences.zh: 」於是軍府將吏上書勸進。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the generals and officials of the military administration submitted a memorial urging him to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: " His generals and staff then submitted a joint memorial urging him to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 十月，延翰建國稱王，而猶稟唐正朔。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Yanhan established his state and declared himself king, yet still acknowledged the Tang calendar.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Yanhan founded his kingdom and proclaimed himself king, while still observing the Tang reign era in official documents.

sentences.zh: 延翰為人長大，美皙如玉，其妻崔氏陋而淫，延翰不能制。

translations.literal: Yanhan was tall in stature, fair and lustrous as jade; his wife the Lady Cui was plain and licentious, and Yanhan could not control her.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhan was tall and handsome, with skin fair as jade. His wife Lady Cui was homely and unchaste, and he could not restrain her.

sentences.zh: 審知喪未期，徹其几筵，又多選良家子為妾。

translations.literal: Before Shenzhi's mourning period had ended, he removed the mourning tables and also selected many daughters of good families as concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Before his father's mourning year was out he cleared away the mourning furnishings and took numerous daughters of respectable families as concubines.

sentences.zh: 崔氏性妒，良家子之美者，輒幽之別室，系以大械，刻木為人手以擊頰，又以鐵錐刺之，一歲中死者八十四人。

translations.literal: The Lady Cui was jealous by nature; whenever a daughter of a good family was beautiful she would confine her in a separate chamber, bind her with heavy fetters, carve a wooden hand to strike her cheeks, and also stab her with iron awls—in one year eighty-four died.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cui was fiercely jealous. Whenever a concubine from a respectable family was beautiful, Cui locked her in a side room, bound her in heavy irons, had a wooden hand carved to slap her face, and stabbed her with iron spikes. Within a single year eighty-four women died at her hands.

sentences.zh: 崔氏後病，見以為祟而卒。

translations.literal: The Lady Cui later fell ill, saw them as malign spirits, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cui later fell ill, believed she was haunted by their spirits, and died.

sentences.zh: 審知養子建州刺史延稟，本姓周氏，自審知時與延翰不葉。

translations.literal: Shenzhi's adopted son Yanbin, prefect of Jian Prefecture, was originally surnamed Zhou; since Shenzhi's time he and Yanhan had not been on good terms.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzhi's adopted son Yanbin, governor of Jianzhou, had been born a Zhou. He and Yanhan had been at odds since Shenzhi's day.

sentences.zh: 延翰立，以其弟延鈞為泉州刺史，延鈞怒。

translations.literal: When Yanhan took power he made his younger brother Yanjun prefect of Quanzhou; Yanjun was angry.
translations.idiomatic: After Yanhan came to power he appointed his younger brother Yanjun prefect of Quanzhou, a slight that enraged Yanjun.

sentences.zh: 二人因謀作亂。

translations.literal: The two men therefore plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The two of them then conspired to rebel.

sentences.zh: 十二月，延稟、延鈞皆以兵入，執延翰殺之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Yanbin and Yanjun both entered with troops, seized Yanhan, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Yanbin and Yanjun marched in with their armies, seized Yanhan, and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 而延鈞立，更名鏻。

translations.literal: Yanjun then took power and changed his name to Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjun then assumed rule and changed his personal name to Lin.

sentences.zh: 鏻，審知次子也。

translations.literal: Lin was Shenzhi's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was Shenzhi's second son.

sentences.zh: 唐即拜鏻節度使，累加檢校太師、中書令，封閩王。

translations.literal: The Tang immediately appointed Lin military governor, repeatedly added the titles of Honorary Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed him as King of Min.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang court promptly appointed Lin military governor and successively honored him with the honorary titles Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffing him as King of Min.

sentences.zh: 初，延稟與鏻之謀殺延翰也，延稟之兵先至，已執延翰而殺之，膽日鏻兵始至，延稟自以養子，推鏻而立之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yanbin and Lin plotted to kill Yanhan, Yanbin's troops arrived first, had already seized Yanhan and killed him; the next day Lin's troops arrived; Yanbin, considering himself an adopted son, yielded and installed Lin.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanbin and Lin had plotted to kill Yanhan, Yanbin's forces arrived first and had already seized and executed him. Lin's troops came only the following day. As an adopted son, Yanbin deferred and set Lin on the throne.

sentences.zh: 延稟還建州，鏻餞於郊，延稟臨訣謂鏻曰：「善繼先誌，毋煩老兄復來！

translations.literal: Yanbin returned to Jian Prefecture; Lin saw him off in the suburbs; at parting Yanbin said to Lin: "Carry on our forefathers' aims well—do not trouble your elder brother to come again!
translations.idiomatic: Yanbin returned to Jianzhou, and Lin escorted him to the outskirts of the city. At their farewell Yanbin told him, "Uphold our forefathers' legacy—and do not make your elder brother march here again!

sentences.zh: 」鏻銜之。

translations.literal: " Lin harbored resentment over this.
translations.idiomatic: " Lin nursed a grudge over the remark.

sentences.zh: 長興二年，延稟率兵擊鏻，攻其西門，使其子繼雄轉海攻其南門，鏻遣王仁達拒之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changxing, Yanbin led troops to attack Lin, assaulting his western gate and sending his son Jixiong by sea to strike the southern gate; Lin dispatched Wang Renda to resist.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changxing, Yanbin marched against Lin, assaulting the western gate while his son Jixiong sailed around to attack the southern gate. Lin sent Wang Renda to meet them.

sentences.zh: 仁達伏甲舟中，偽立白幟請降，繼雄信之，登舟，伏兵發，刺殺之，梟其首西門，其兵見之皆潰去，延稟見執。

translations.literal: Renda hid armored men in the boats, falsely raised white banners to request surrender; Jixiong believed him, boarded the boat, the ambush sprang forth and stabbed him to death; his head was displayed at the western gate; his troops, seeing it, all fled; Yanbin was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Renda concealed armored men aboard his vessels and hoisted white flags in a feigned surrender. Jixiong believed him, came aboard, and the hidden soldiers leaped out and killed him. Renda displayed Jixiong's head at the western gate; at the sight his army broke and fled. Yanbin was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 鏻誚之曰：「予不能繼先誌，果煩老兄復來！

translations.literal: Lin mocked him, saying: "I could not carry on our forefathers' aims—so it truly did trouble my elder brother to come again!
translations.idiomatic: Lin taunted him: "So I failed to uphold our forefathers' legacy, and your elder brother really did have to come again!

sentences.zh: 」延廩不能對，遂殺之。

translations.literal: " Yanbin could not reply and was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanbin had no answer and was executed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 延稟子繼升守建州，聞敗，奔於錢塘。

translations.literal: Yanbin's son Jisheng held Jian Prefecture; hearing of the defeat, he fled to Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbin's son Jisheng was defending Jianzhou. When he heard of the defeat he fled to Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 鏻好鬼神、道家之說，道士陳守元以左道見信，建寶皇宮以居之。

translations.literal: Lin favored spirits and ghosts and Daoist teachings; the Daoist Chen Shouyuan, through heterodox arts, won his trust, and he built the Precious Imperial Palace for him to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was devoted to spirits and Daoist lore. The Daoist Chen Shouyuan won his confidence through occult practices, and Lin built the Precious Imperial Palace for him to live in.

sentences.zh: 守元謂鏻曰：「寶皇命王少避其位，後當為六十年天子。

translations.literal: Shouyuan said to Lin: "The Precious Emperor commands the king briefly to yield his seat; afterward he shall be Son of Heaven for sixty years.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyuan told Lin, "The Precious Emperor orders you to step aside for a time. Afterward you will reign as Son of Heaven for sixty years.

sentences.zh: 」鏻欣然遜位，命其子繼鵬權主府事。

translations.literal: " Lin gladly abdicated and ordered his son Jipeng to administer the prefectural affairs provisionally.
translations.idiomatic: " Delighted, Lin abdicated and put his son Jipeng in charge of government affairs.

sentences.zh: 既而復位，遣守元問寶皇：「六十年後將安歸？

translations.literal: He then resumed the throne and sent Shouyuan to ask the Precious Emperor: "After sixty years, whither shall I go?
translations.idiomatic: He soon took the throne back and sent Shouyuan to inquire of the Precious Emperor, "Where shall I go when the sixty years are done?

sentences.zh: 」守元傳寶皇語曰：「六十年後，當為大羅仙人。

translations.literal: " Shouyuan relayed the Precious Emperor's words: "After sixty years you shall become a Great Canopy Immortal.
translations.idiomatic: " Shouyuan brought back the answer: "After sixty years you will become an immortal of the Great Canopy Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」鏻乃即皇帝位，受冊於寶皇，以黃龍見真封宅，改元為龍啟，國號閩。

translations.literal: " Lin then assumed the imperial throne, received investiture from the Precious Emperor, took the Yellow Dragon Manifest Truth Sealed Residence as his dwelling, changed the era name to Dragon Inception, and made the state name Min.
translations.idiomatic: " Lin thereupon declared himself emperor, received his mandate from the Precious Emperor, took up residence in the Yellow Dragon Manifest Truth palace, adopted the era name Dragon Inception, and proclaimed the state of Min.

sentences.zh: 追謚審知為昭武孝皇帝，廟號太祖，立五廟，置百官，以福州為長樂府。

translations.literal: He posthumously titled Shenzhi Emperor Zhaowu Xiaohuang, temple name Taizu, established five ancestral temples, installed the full bureaucracy, and made Fuzhou the Changle Metropolitan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously honored Shenzhi as Emperor Zhaowu the Filial, with the temple name Taizu, established five ancestral temples, appointed a full court, and renamed Fuzhou the Changle metropolitan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 而閩地狹，國用不足，以中軍使薛文傑為國計使。

translations.literal: But Min's territory was narrow and state revenue insufficient; he made the Central Army Commissioner Xue Wenjie national revenue commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Min's territory was small and revenues scarce, so he appointed the Central Army Commissioner Xue Wenjie national revenue commissioner.

sentences.zh: 文傑多察民間陰事，致富人以罪，而籍沒其貲以佐用，閩人皆怨。

translations.literal: Wenjie often investigated private matters among the people, charged the wealthy with crimes, and confiscated their property to supplement expenditures; all the people of Min resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjie pried into private affairs throughout the realm, framed wealthy families on trumped-up charges, and confiscated their goods to fill the treasury. The people of Min hated him.

sentences.zh: 又薦妖巫徐彥，曰：「陛下左右多奸臣，不質諸鬼神，將為亂。

translations.literal: He also recommended the sorcerer Xu Yan, saying: "Around Your Majesty are many treacherous ministers; if you do not verify them through spirits and ghosts, there will be rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended the sorcerer Xu Yan, saying, "Your Majesty is surrounded by traitors. Unless you test them through spirits, rebellion will follow.

sentences.zh: 」鏻使彥視鬼於宮中。

translations.literal: " Lin had Yan observe ghosts within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: " Lin ordered Yan to divine for ghosts within the palace.

sentences.zh: 文傑與內樞密使吳英有隙，英病在告，文傑謂英曰：「上以公居近密，而屢以疾告，將罷公。

translations.literal: Wenjie had a rift with the Inner Palace Military Affairs Commissioner Wu Ying; Ying was ill on leave; Wenjie said to Ying: "The emperor, seeing that you hold a post close to the inner quarters yet repeatedly report illness, will dismiss you.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjie bore a grudge against the Inner Palace Military Affairs Commissioner Wu Ying. While Ying was on sick leave Wenjie told him, "The emperor thinks that because you hold a post at court you ought not keep pleading illness. He means to remove you.

sentences.zh: 」英曰：「奈何？

translations.literal: " Ying said: "What is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: " Ying asked, "What can I do?

sentences.zh: 」文傑因教英曰：「即上遣人問公疾，當言『頭痛而已，無他苦也。

translations.literal: " Wenjie then instructed Ying: "When the emperor next sends someone to inquire about your illness, you should say, 'Only a headache—no other affliction.
translations.idiomatic: " Wenjie coached him: "When the emperor sends someone to ask after your health, say only, 'A headache—nothing more serious than that.

sentences.zh: 』」英以為然。

translations.literal: '" Ying thought this sound.
translations.idiomatic: '" Ying agreed that this was wise counsel.

sentences.zh: 明日，諷鏻使巫視英疾，巫言：「入北廟，見英為崇順王所訊，曰：『汝何敢謀反？

translations.literal: The next day he prompted Lin to have the sorcerer examine Ying's illness; the sorcerer said: "Entering the northern temple, I saw Ying interrogated by King Chongshun, who said: 'How dare you plot rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: The next day he persuaded Lin to have the sorcerer divine Ying's illness. The sorcerer reported, "In the northern temple I saw Ying questioned by King Chongshun, who demanded, 'How dare you plot rebellion?

sentences.zh: 』以金槌擊其首。

translations.literal: ' He struck his head with a golden mallet.
translations.idiomatic: ' He struck his head with a golden mallet.

sentences.zh: 」鏻以語文傑，文傑曰：「未可信也，宜問其疾如何。

translations.literal: " Lin reported this to Wenjie; Wenjie said: "This cannot yet be trusted; you should ask what his illness is like.
translations.idiomatic: " Lin told Wenjie what the sorcerer had said. Wenjie replied, "That alone proves nothing. Ask what his illness actually is.

sentences.zh: 」鏻遣人問之，英曰：「頭痛。

translations.literal: " Lin sent someone to inquire; Ying said: "A headache.
translations.idiomatic: " Lin sent an envoy to Ying, who answered, "A headache.

sentences.zh: 」鏻以為然，即以英下獄，命文傑劾之，英自誣伏，見殺。

translations.literal: " Lin believed it; he immediately imprisoned Ying, ordered Wenjie to prosecute him; Ying confessed to the false charge and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: " Lin took this as confirmation, threw Ying into prison, and ordered Wenjie to prosecute him. Ying confessed to the fabricated charge and was executed.

sentences.zh: 英嘗主閩兵，得其軍士心，軍士聞英死，皆怒。

translations.literal: Ying had once commanded Min's troops and won the soldiers' hearts; when the soldiers heard Ying was dead, all were enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Ying had once commanded the Min armies and won the soldiers' loyalty. When the troops learned of his death they were furious.

sentences.zh: 是歲，吳人攻建州，鏻遣其將王延宗救之，兵士在道不肯進，曰：「得文傑乃進。

translations.literal: That year the Wu people attacked Jian Prefecture; Lin sent his general Wang Yancong to rescue it; the soldiers on the march refused to advance, saying: "We advance only when we get Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Wu attacked Jianzhou. Lin sent his general Wang Yancong to relieve the city, but the troops on the march refused to go forward, crying, "Hand over Wenjie, then we march!

sentences.zh: 」鏻惜之不與，其子繼鵬請與之以紓難，乃以檻車送文傑軍中。

translations.literal: " Lin was reluctant and would not give him up; his son Jipeng asked to surrender him to ease the crisis; they then sent Wenjie in a caged cart to the army.
translations.idiomatic: " Lin was loath to surrender him. His son Jipeng urged that Wenjie be given up to avert disaster, and Wenjie was sent to the army in a prison cart.

sentences.zh: 文傑善數術，自占云：「過三日可無患。

translations.literal: Wenjie was skilled in numerology; he divined for himself and said: "After three days I shall be free of trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjie was skilled in divination and cast his own fortune, saying, "In three days I shall be safe.

sentences.zh: 」送者聞之，疾馳二日而至，軍士踴躍，磔文傑於市，閩人爭以瓦石投之，臠食立盡。

translations.literal: " The escorts heard this and galloped hard, arriving in two days; the soldiers leaped for joy, dismembered Wenjie in the marketplace, and the people of Min vied to pelt him with tiles and stones until his flesh was devoured on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: " Hearing this, the escorts spurred their horses and reached the army in two days instead of three. The soldiers erupted in joy, dismembered Wenjie in the marketplace, and the people of Min pelted his body with tiles and stones until every scrap of flesh was gone.

sentences.zh: 明日，鏻使者至，赦之，已不及。

translations.literal: The next day Lin's envoy arrived with a pardon—it was already too late.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Lin's messenger arrived with an order of pardon, but it was too late.

sentences.zh: 初，文傑為鏻造檻車，以謂古制疏闊，乃更其制，令上下通，中以鐵芒內向，動輒觸之，既成，首被其毒。

translations.literal: Earlier Wenjie had built a caged cart for Lin, considering the ancient design too loose; he therefore redesigned it so that top and bottom communicated, with iron spikes pointing inward in the middle—at the slightest movement one was pricked—and when it was finished he was the first to suffer from it.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjie had once designed a prison cart for Lin, finding the old model too loose. He redesigned it with open top and bottom and inward-pointing iron spikes so that any movement drew blood. When it was finished he became its first victim.

sentences.zh: 龍啟三年，改元永和。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dragon Inception he changed the era name to Eternal Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dragon Inception he adopted the era name Eternal Harmony.

sentences.zh: 王仁達為鏻殺延稟有功，而典親兵，鏻心忌之，嘗問仁達曰：「趙高指鹿為馬，以愚二世，果有之邪？

translations.literal: Wang Renda had merit for killing Yanbin on Lin's behalf and commanded the personal guard; Lin harbored suspicion in his heart and once asked Renda: "When Zhao Gao called a deer a horse to deceive the Second Emperor—did that truly happen?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Renda had distinguished himself by killing Yanbin and now commanded the imperial guard. Lin grew jealous and once asked him, "Did Zhao Gao really point to a deer and call it a horse to deceive the Second Emperor?

sentences.zh: 」仁達曰：「秦二世愚，故高指鹿為馬，非高能愚二世也。

translations.literal: " Renda said: "The Second Emperor of Qin was foolish, so Gao called a deer a horse—it was not that Gao could make the Second Emperor foolish.
translations.idiomatic: " Renda replied, "The Second Emperor of Qin was a fool, which is why Gao could call a deer a horse. Gao did not make the emperor foolish—the emperor was already foolish.

sentences.zh: 今陛下聰明，朝廷官不滿百，起居動靜，陛下皆知之，敢有作威福者，族滅之而已。

translations.literal: Today Your Majesty is wise; the court officials number fewer than a hundred; your comings and goings and every movement Your Majesty knows—who would dare wield power for private ends? Exterminate his clan, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is intelligent, the court has fewer than a hundred officials, and you know every movement at court. Anyone who dared abuse his power could simply be exterminated along with his clan.

sentences.zh: 」鏻慚，賜與金帛慰安之。

translations.literal: " Lin was ashamed and bestowed gold and silk to comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: " Lin was abashed and rewarded him with gold and silk to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 退而謂人曰：「仁達智略，在吾世可用，不可遺後世患。

translations.literal: Afterward he said to others: "Renda's wisdom and stratagems can be used in my lifetime; he must not be left as a trouble for later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he told his attendants, "Renda's talent is useful while I live, but he must not be left as a threat to my heirs.

sentences.zh: 」卒誣以罪殺之。

translations.literal: " In the end he framed him on a charge and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he fabricated charges and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 鏻妻早卒，繼室金氏賢而不見答。

translations.literal: Lin's wife died early; his second wife the Lady Jin was worthy yet received no favor.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's first wife died young. His second wife, Lady Jin, was virtuous but went unloved.

sentences.zh: 審知婢金鳳，姓陳氏，鏻嬖之，遂立以為後。

translations.literal: Shenzhi's maid Golden Phoenix, surnamed Chen, Lin favored and then installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Golden Phoenix, a maid of Shenzhi's from the Chen clan, became Lin's favorite and was raised to empress.

sentences.zh: 初，鏻有嬖吏歸守明者，以色見倖，號歸郎，鏻後得風疾，陳氏與歸郎奸。

translations.literal: Earlier Lin had a favored clerk Gui Shouming who won favor through his looks and was called Lord Gui; Lin later contracted wind illness, and the Lady Chen and Lord Gui committed adultery.
translations.idiomatic: Lin once kept a favorite clerk named Gui Shouming, who won his affection by his beauty and was nicknamed Lord Gui. After Lin fell ill with paralysis, Empress Chen and Lord Gui became lovers.

sentences.zh: 又有百工院使李可殷，因歸郎以通陳氏。

translations.literal: There was also the Hundred Crafts Bureau Commissioner Li Keyin, who through Lord Gui gained access to the Lady Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyin, commissioner of the Hundred Crafts Bureau, also gained access to the empress through Lord Gui.

sentences.zh: 鏻命錦工作九龍帳，國人歌曰：「誰謂九龍帳，惟貯一歸郎！」

translations.literal: Lin ordered the brocade workers to make a Nine Dragons canopy; the people sang: "Who says the Nine Dragons canopy holds anything but one Lord Gui!"
translations.idiomatic: Lin ordered the brocade workshops to weave a Nine Dragons canopy. The people sang, "They call it the Nine Dragons canopy, but it holds only Lord Gui!"

sentences.zh: 鏻婢春燕有色，其子繼鵬蒸之，鏻已病，繼鵬因陳氏以求春燕，鏻怏怏與之。

translations.literal: Lin's maid Spring Swallow was beautiful; his son Jipeng took her as a concubine; Lin was already ill; Jipeng through the Lady Chen asked for Spring Swallow; Lin reluctantly gave her to him.
translations.idiomatic: Spring Swallow, a maid in Lin's household, was beautiful. His son Jipeng took her as a concubine. Already gravely ill, Lin yielded her to Jipeng at Empress Chen's urging, though he did so with bitter reluctance.

sentences.zh: 其次子繼韜怒，謀殺繼鵬，繼鵬懼，與皇城使李仿圖之。

translations.literal: His second son Jitao was angry and plotted to kill Jipeng; Jipeng was afraid and, with the Imperial City Commissioner Li Fang, plotted against him.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Jitao, enraged, plotted to kill Jipeng. Jipeng, in fear, conspired with the Imperial City Commissioner Li Fang.

sentences.zh: 是歲十月，鏻饗軍於大酺殿，坐中昏然，言見延稟來，仿以為鏻病已甚，乃令壯士先殺李可殷於家。

translations.literal: That year in the tenth month Lin feasted the army in the Great Revelry Hall; mid-feast he grew dazed and said he saw Yanbin coming; Fang thought Lin's illness was already grave and ordered stalwart men first to kill Li Keyin at his home.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year Lin feasted his troops in the Great Revelry Hall. Midway through the banquet he fell into a stupor and cried that Yanbin had come for him. Fang judged Lin's illness beyond recovery and sent bravos to kill Li Keyin at his home.

sentences.zh: 明日晨朝，鏻無恙，問仿殺可殷何罪，仿懼而出，與繼鵬率皇城衛士而入。

translations.literal: The next morning at court audience Lin was unharmed and asked Fang what crime Keyin had committed to be killed; Fang fled in fear and, with Jipeng, led the Imperial City guards inside.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning Lin appeared at court unharmed and demanded to know what crime had justified Keyin's murder. Fang fled in terror and, with Jipeng, led the Imperial City guards into the palace.

sentences.zh: 鏻聞鼓噪聲，走匿九龍帳中，衛士刺之不殂，宮人不忍其苦，為絕之。

translations.literal: Hearing the clamor of drums, Lin ran and hid in the Nine Dragons canopy; the guards stabbed him but did not kill him; palace women could not bear his suffering and finished him off.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the uproar, Lin fled into the Nine Dragons canopy. The guards stabbed him but failed to kill him outright, and the palace women, unable to bear his agony, finished him off.

sentences.zh: 繼韜及陳後、歸郎皆為仿所殺。

translations.literal: Jitao, Empress Chen, and Lord Gui were all killed by Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Jitao, Empress Chen, and Lord Gui were all killed by Fang.

sentences.zh: 鏻立十年見殺，謚曰惠皇帝，廟號太宗。

translations.literal: Lin had reigned ten years when he was killed; his posthumous title was Emperor Hui, temple name Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Lin had ruled ten years when he was murdered. He was posthumously titled Emperor Hui, with the temple name Taizong.

sentences.zh: 繼鵬，鏻長子也。

translations.literal: Jipeng was Lin's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Jipeng was Lin's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 既立，更名昶，改元通文，以李仿判六軍諸衛事。

translations.literal: Once established he changed his name to Chang, altered the era name to Pervading Culture, and made Li Fang overseer of the Six Armies and all guards.
translations.idiomatic: On taking the throne he changed his personal name to Chang, adopted the era name Pervading Culture, and appointed Li Fang commander of the Six Armies and palace guards.

sentences.zh: 仿有弒君之罪，既立昶，而心常自疑，多養死士以為備。

translations.literal: Fang bore the crime of regicide; though Chang was now enthroned, he constantly doubted himself in his heart and kept many death-defying warriors as a precaution.
translations.idiomatic: Fang had murdered his sovereign. Even after Chang's enthronement he lived in constant fear and maintained a large corps of devoted fighters as insurance.

sentences.zh: 昶患之，因大享軍，伏甲擒仿殺之，梟其首於市。

translations.literal: Chang resented this; he therefore held a great feast for the army, hid armored men, seized Fang and killed him, and displayed his head in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Chang feared Fang's power. At a grand military feast he concealed armed men, seized Fang, and executed him, then displayed his head in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 仿部曲千人叛，燒啟聖門，奪仿首，奔於錢塘。

translations.literal: A thousand of Fang's personal troops rebelled, burned the Gate of Enlightened Sagacity, seized Fang's head, and fled to Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand of Fang's personal troops mutinied, burned the Gate of Enlightened Sagacity, recovered their commander's head, and fled to Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 晉天福二年，昶遣使朝貢京師，高祖遣散騎常侍盧損冊昶閩王，拜其子繼恭臨海郡王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianfu of Jin, Chang sent envoys to the capital to present tribute; the founding emperor dispatched the Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Lu Sun to invest Chang as King of Min and appoint his son Jigong Prince of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianfu, Chang sent tribute envoys to the Jin capital. Emperor Gaozu dispatched Lu Sun, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, to invest Chang as King of Min and appoint his son Jigong Prince of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 損至閩，昶稱疾不見，令繼恭主之。

translations.literal: When Sun reached Min, Chang claimed illness and would not see him, ordering Jigong to receive him in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun arrived in Min, Chang pleaded illness and refused an audience, leaving Jigong to receive him.

sentences.zh: 又遣中書舍人劉乙勞損於館，乙衣冠偉然，騶僮甚盛。

translations.literal: He also sent the Secretariat Drafter Liu Yi to entertain Sun at the guesthouse; Yi was imposing in cap and robes, with a very grand escort of grooms and attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Secretariat Drafter Liu Yi to entertain Sun at the guesthouse. Yi appeared in magnificent dress with an imposing retinue of grooms and servants.

sentences.zh: 他日損遇乙於途，布衣芒屩而已，損使人誚之曰：「鳳閣舍人，何偪下之甚也！

translations.literal: Another day Sun met Yi on the road wearing only plain cloth and straw sandals; Sun sent someone to mock him, saying: "Phoenix Pavilion drafter—how extremely you demean yourself!
translations.idiomatic: Another day Sun met Yi on the road dressed in plain cloth and straw sandals. Sun sent a man to taunt him: "Phoenix Pavilion drafter, how far you have lowered yourself!

sentences.zh: 」乙羞愧，以手掩面而走。

translations.literal: " Yi was ashamed and, covering his face with his hands, fled.
translations.idiomatic: " Mortified, Yi covered his face and fled.

sentences.zh: 昶聞之，怒損侵辱之，損還，昶無所答。

translations.literal: When Chang heard of this he was angry that Sun had insulted them; Sun returned, and Chang made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was furious that Sun had humiliated his envoy. Sun returned home, and Chang offered no response to the court.

sentences.zh: 而其子繼恭遣其佐鄭元弼隨損至京師貢方物，致書晉大臣，述昶意求以敵國禮相往來。

translations.literal: Yet his son Jigong sent his aide Zheng Yuanbi to follow Sun to the capital with local products as tribute, writing to Jin ministers to convey Chang's wish to treat each other with the ceremonies due between equal states.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile his son Jigong sent aide Zheng Yuanbi to accompany Sun to the capital with tribute goods and a letter to Jin ministers asking that Min and Jin exchange embassies as equal states.

sentences.zh: 高祖怒其不遜，下詔暴其罪，歸其貢物不納。

translations.literal: The founding emperor was angry at their insolence, issued an edict exposing their crimes, and returned their tribute goods without accepting them.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was enraged by this insolence. He issued an edict listing their offenses and returned their tribute unaccepted.

sentences.zh: 兵部員外郎李知損上書請籍沒其物而禁錮使者，於是以元弼下獄。

translations.literal: The Vice Director of the Ministry of War Li Zhisun memorialized requesting confiscation of their goods and imprisonment of the envoys; Yuanbi was therefore thrown into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhisun, Vice Director of the Ministry of War, memorialized asking that the goods be confiscated and the envoys imprisoned. Yuanbi was thrown into jail.

sentences.zh: 獄具引見，元弼俯伏曰：「昶，夷貊之君，不知禮義，陛下方示大信，以來遠人，臣將命無狀，願伏斧钅質，以贖昶罪。

translations.literal: When the case was complete he was brought before the throne; Yuanbi prostrated himself and said: "Chang is a barbarian lord who knows nothing of ritual and righteousness; Your Majesty is just now displaying great faith to draw distant peoples; I discharged my commission disgracefully and wish to submit to the axe to atone for Chang's offense.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was concluded Yuanbi was brought before the throne. He prostrated himself and said, "Chang is a barbarian ruler who knows nothing of propriety. Your Majesty is showing great faith to draw distant peoples to your court. I have failed in my mission and beg to accept the axe in Chang's stead.

sentences.zh: 」高祖乃赦元弼，遣歸。

translations.literal: " The founding emperor then pardoned Yuanbi and sent him home.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu pardoned Yuanbi and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 昶亦好巫，拜道士譚紫霄為正一先生，又拜陳守元為天師，而妖人林興以巫見幸，事無大小，興輒以寶皇語命之而後行。

translations.literal: Chang also favored sorcery, invested the Daoist Tan Zixiao as Lord of the Orthodox Unity, and again invested Chen Shouyuan as Celestial Master; the sorcerer Lin Xing won favor through witchcraft—matters great and small, Xing would issue commands in the Precious Emperor's words before they were carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Chang also dabbled in sorcery, naming the Daoist Tan Zixiao Lord of Orthodox Unity and Chen Shouyuan Celestial Master. The sorcerer Lin Xing won his favor, and no matter great or small was undertaken until Xing pronounced the Precious Emperor's command.

sentences.zh: 守元教昶起三清臺三層，以黃金數千斤鑄寶皇及元始天尊、太上老君像，日焚龍腦、薰陸諸香數斤，作樂於臺下，晝夜聲不輟，雲如此可求大還丹。

translations.literal: Shouyuan taught Chang to build a three-tiered Three Pure Ones Terrace, cast images of the Precious Emperor, the Primordial Heavenly Worthy, and the Supreme Lord Lao with several thousand jin of gold, burn several jin daily of dragon-brain, spikenard, and other incense, and make music below the terrace day and night without cease, saying that thus one could obtain the Great Reverted Elixir.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyuan persuaded Chang to erect a three-tiered Terrace of the Three Pure Ones and cast statues of the Precious Emperor, the Primordial Heavenly Worthy, and the Supreme Lord Lao from thousands of jin of gold. Each day several jin of dragon-brain, spikenard, and other incense were burned while music played below the terrace without cease, day and night, on the promise that the Great Reverted Elixir could be obtained this way.

sentences.zh: 三年夏，虹見其宮中，林興傳神言：「此宗室將為亂之兆也。

translations.literal: In the summer of the third year a rainbow appeared in his palace; Lin Xing relayed a spirit message: "This is an omen that the imperial clan will bring rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the third year a rainbow appeared in the palace. Lin Xing relayed a spirit message: "This is an omen that the imperial clan will rebel.

sentences.zh: 」乃命興率壯士殺審知子延武、延望及其子五人。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Xing to lead stalwart men to kill Shenzhi's sons Yanwu and Yanwang and their five sons.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered Xing to lead bravos to kill Shenzhi's sons Yanwu and Yanwang along with five of their sons.

sentences.zh: 後興事敗，亦被殺。

translations.literal: Later Xing's affair failed and he too was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xing's plot collapsed he too was executed.

sentences.zh: 而昶愈惑亂，立父婢春燕為淑妃，後立以為皇后。

translations.literal: Yet Chang grew ever more confused and disorderly; he installed his father's maid Spring Swallow as Pure Consort and later raised her to empress.
translations.idiomatic: Chang grew only more erratic. He made his father's maid Spring Swallow a Pure Consort and later elevated her to empress.

sentences.zh: 又遣醫人陳究以空名堂牒賣官。

translations.literal: He also sent the physician Chen Jiu to sell offices with blank Hall memorials.
translations.idiomatic: He also had the physician Chen Jiu sell offices using blank appointment documents.

sentences.zh: 昶弟繼嚴判六軍諸衛事，昶疑而罷之，代以季弟繼鏞，而募勇士為宸衛都以自衛，其賜予給賞，獨厚於他軍。

translations.literal: Chang's brother Jiyan oversaw the Six Armies and all guards; Chang suspected him and dismissed him, replacing him with his youngest brother Jiyong; he recruited stalwart men for the Imperial Guard Command to protect himself, whose grants and rewards alone were richer than the other armies.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's brother Jiyan commanded the Six Armies and palace guards. Chang suspected him, removed him, and replaced him with his youngest brother Jiyong. He then recruited stalwart men into an Imperial Guard Command for his personal protection and lavished on them rewards richer than those given any other unit.

sentences.zh: 控鶴都將連重遇、拱宸都將朱文進，皆以此怒激其軍。

translations.literal: The Crane-Control Commanders Lian Chongyu and the Arch-Palace Commanders Zhu Wenjin both roused their troops to anger over this.
translations.idiomatic: The Crane-Control commander Lian Chongyu and the Arch-Palace commander Zhu Wenjin incited their troops to fury over this favoritism.

sentences.zh: 是歲夏，術者言昶宮中當有災，昶徙南宮避災，而宮中火，昶疑重遇軍士縱火。

translations.literal: That summer diviners said disaster would strike within Chang's palace; Chang moved to the Southern Palace to avoid calamity, but fire broke out in the palace; Chang suspected soldiers of Chongyu's command had set the blaze.
translations.idiomatic: That summer diviners warned of disaster in the palace. Chang moved to the Southern Palace to escape it, but fire broke out anyway. Chang suspected soldiers under Chongyu of arson.

sentences.zh: 內學士陳郯素以便佞為昶所親信，昶以火事語之，郯反以告重遇。

translations.literal: The Inner Academician Chen Tan had long won Chang's trust through flattery; Chang spoke to him about the fire, and Tan in turn informed Chongyu.
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Academician Chen Tan had long won Chang's trust through flattery. Chang confided his suspicions about the fire to Tan, who promptly warned Chongyu.

sentences.zh: 重遇懼，夜率衛士縱火焚南宮，昶挾愛姬、子弟、黃門衛士斬關而出，宿於野次。

translations.literal: Chongyu was afraid; that night he led guards to set fire and burn the Southern Palace; Chang took his favorite consorts, sons, and eunuch guards, cut through the gates and fled, lodging in the open countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Chongyu led his guards that night to burn the Southern Palace. Chang fled with his favorite consorts, sons, and eunuch guards, cutting his way through the gates to camp in the open countryside.

sentences.zh: 重遇迎延義立之。

translations.literal: Chongyu welcomed Yanyi and installed him.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyu welcomed Yanyi and set him on the throne.

sentences.zh: 延義令其子繼業率兵襲昶，及之；

translations.literal: Yanyi ordered his son Jiye to lead troops in pursuit of Chang and overtook him;
translations.idiomatic: Yanyi sent his son Jiye with troops to pursue Chang and overtook him.

sentences.zh: 射殺數人，昶知不免，擲弓於地，繼業執而殺之，及其妻、子皆死無遺類。

translations.literal: several were shot dead; Chang knew he could not escape, cast his bow to the ground; Jiye seized and killed him, and his wife and sons all died without a survivor.
translations.idiomatic: Several of Chang's party were shot down. Seeing escape was impossible, Chang threw down his bow. Jiye seized him and killed him, and his wife and sons were slaughtered to the last person.

sentences.zh: 延義立，謚昶曰康宗。

translations.literal: Yanyi took the throne and gave Chang the posthumous title Sovereign Kang.
translations.idiomatic: With Yanyi enthroned, Chang was posthumously titled Sovereign Kang.

sentences.zh: 延義，審知少子也。

translations.literal: Yanyi was Shenzhi's youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyi was Shenzhi's youngest son.

sentences.zh: 既立，更名曦，遣使者朝貢於晉，改元永隆。

translations.literal: Once established he changed his name to Xi, sent envoys to present tribute to Jin, and altered the era name to Eternal Ascent.
translations.idiomatic: On taking power he changed his personal name to Xi, sent tribute envoys to Jin, and adopted the era name Eternal Ascent.

sentences.zh: 鑄大鐵錢，以一當十。

translations.literal: He cast large iron coins valued at ten to one.
translations.idiomatic: He cast large iron coins, each reckoned as ten ordinary coins.

sentences.zh: 曦自昶世倔強難制，昶相王倓每抑折之，曦亦憚倓，不敢有所發。

translations.literal: Xi had been stubborn and hard to control since Chang's reign; Chang's chancellor Wang Tan often repressed and checked him, and Xi also feared Tan and dared not act out.
translations.idiomatic: Xi had been unruly and defiant even under Chang. Chang's chancellor Wang Tan had repeatedly reined him in, and Xi feared Tan enough to keep his resentment hidden.

sentences.zh: 新羅遣使聘閩以寶劍，昶舉以示倓曰：「此將何為？

translations.literal: Silla sent envoys to Min with a precious sword as a gift; Chang held it up to show Tan and said: "What is this for?
translations.idiomatic: Silla sent envoys to Min bearing a precious sword. Chang held it up for Tan and asked, "What do you suppose this is for?

sentences.zh: 」倓曰：「不忠不孝者，斬之。

translations.literal: " Tan said: "To behead the disloyal and unfilial.
translations.idiomatic: " Tan replied, "To behead the disloyal and unfilial.

sentences.zh: 」曦居旁色變。

translations.literal: " Xi, standing nearby, changed color.
translations.idiomatic: " Xi, standing nearby, turned pale.

sentences.zh: 曦既立，而新羅復獻劍，曦思倓前言，而倓已死，命發冢戮其屍，倓面如生，血流被體。

translations.literal: Once Xi was enthroned Silla again presented a sword; Xi recalled Tan's earlier words, but Tan was already dead; he ordered the tomb opened and the corpse flogged; Tan's face was as if alive and blood flowed over his body.
translations.idiomatic: After Xi took the throne Silla sent another sword. Remembering Tan's earlier remark, and learning Tan was dead, Xi ordered his tomb opened and his corpse flogged. Tan's face looked as if he were alive, and blood streamed over his body.

sentences.zh: 泉州刺史余廷英嘗矯曦命掠取良家子，曦怒，召下御史劾之。

translations.literal: The Quanzhou prefect Yu Tingying had once forged Xi's orders to seize daughters of good families; Xi was angry and summoned the censors to prosecute him.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhou prefect Yu Tingying had forged Xi's orders to seize daughters of respectable families. Xi was furious and ordered the censors to prosecute him.

sentences.zh: 廷英進買宴錢千萬，曦曰：「皇后土貢何在？

translations.literal: Tingying presented ten million in banquet-purchase money; Xi said: "Where is the empress's local tribute?
translations.idiomatic: Tingying offered ten million cash to buy his way out of prosecution. Xi demanded, "Where is the empress's tribute?

sentences.zh: 」廷英又獻皇后錢千萬，乃得不劾。

translations.literal: " Tingying again presented ten million for the empress, and only then escaped prosecution.
translations.idiomatic: " Tingying paid another ten million for the empress and was spared prosecution.

sentences.zh: 曦嘗嫁女，朝士有不賀者笞之。

translations.literal: When Xi married off a daughter, court officials who did not offer congratulations were flogged.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi married off a daughter, any court official who failed to offer congratulations was flogged.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞劉贊坐不糾舉，將加笞，諫議大夫鄭元弼切諫，曦謂元弼曰：「卿何如魏鄭公，乃敢強諫！

translations.literal: The Censor-in-Chief Liu Zan was charged with failing to impeach and was about to be flogged; the Remonstrance Counselor Zheng Yuanbi remonstrated forcefully; Xi said to Yuanbi: "In what way are you like Duke Wei of Zheng that you dare remonstrate so strongly!
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Liu Zan was charged with failing to impeach the offenders and was about to be flogged. Remonstrance Counselor Zheng Yuanbi protested sharply. Xi told him, "What makes you think you are Duke Wei of Zheng that you dare remonstrate so boldly?

sentences.zh: 」元弼曰：「陛下似唐太宗，臣為魏鄭公可矣。

translations.literal: " Yuanbi said: "Your Majesty resembles Emperor Taizong of Tang; I may well serve as Duke Wei of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuanbi replied, "If Your Majesty resembles Emperor Taizong of Tang, then I may well play the part of Duke Wei of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 」曦喜，乃釋贊不笞。

translations.literal: " Xi was pleased and released Zan without flogging.
translations.idiomatic: " Xi was amused and spared Zan the flogging.

sentences.zh: 曦弟延政為建州節度使，封富沙王，自曦立，不葉，數舉兵相攻，曦由此惡其宗室，多以事誅之。

translations.literal: Xi's brother Yanzheng was military governor of Jian Prefecture, enfeoffed as Prince of Fusha; since Xi's enthronement they were not on good terms and repeatedly raised troops against each other; Xi therefore hated his clan and killed many of them on various charges.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's brother Yanzheng, military governor of Jianzhou and Prince of Fusha, had been at odds with him since Xi's enthronement and repeatedly marched against him. Xi came to hate his own clan and executed many kinsmen on one pretext or another.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫黃峻舁櫬詣朝堂極諫，曦怒，貶峻漳州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: The Remonstrance Counselor Huang Jun carried his coffin to the court hall and remonstrated to the utmost; Xi was angry and demoted Jun to Registrar of Zhang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Counselor Huang Jun carried his own coffin into court and remonstrated to the limit. Xi was enraged and demoted him to registrar in Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 校書郎陳光逸上書疏曦過惡五十餘事，曦命衛士鞭之百而不死，以繩系頸，掛於木，久而乃絕。

translations.literal: The Proofreader Chen Guangyi submitted a memorial listing more than fifty of Xi's faults and crimes; Xi ordered guards to flog him a hundred strokes without killing him, tied a rope around his neck, hung him from a tree, and only after a long while did he die.
translations.idiomatic: Proofreader Chen Guangyi submitted a memorial listing more than fifty of Xi's crimes. Xi ordered guards to flog him a hundred strokes without killing him, then bound a rope around his neck and hung him from a tree until he finally died.

sentences.zh: 國計使陳匡范增算商之法以獻，曦曰：「匡範人中寶也。

translations.literal: The National Revenue Commissioner Chen Kuangfan presented a plan to increase merchant tax assessments; Xi said: "Kuangfan is a treasure among men.
translations.idiomatic: National Revenue Commissioner Chen Kuangfan proposed heavier merchant taxes. Xi declared, "Kuangfan is a treasure among men.

sentences.zh: 」已而歲入不登其數，乃借於民以足之，匡範以憂死。

translations.literal: " Before long the year's revenue did not reach the target figure, so they borrowed from the people to make it up; Kuangfan died of anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: " When annual revenue still fell short, officials borrowed from the people to make up the deficit. Kuangfan died of anxiety.

sentences.zh: 其後知其借於民也，剖棺斷屍，棄之水中。

translations.literal: Later, learning that the shortfall had been made up by borrowing from the people, he opened the coffin, dismembered the corpse, and cast it into the water.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi later learned the deficit had been covered by forced loans from the people, he had Kuangfan's coffin opened, the corpse dismembered, and the remains thrown into the river.

sentences.zh: 曦性既淫虐，而妻李氏悍而酗酒，賢妃尚氏有色而寵。

translations.literal: Xi's nature was already lewd and cruel; his wife the Lady Li was fierce and given to heavy drinking; the Worthy Consort the Lady Shang was beautiful and favored.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was by nature lewd and cruel. His wife Lady Li was fierce and a heavy drinker, while the Worthy Consort Lady Shang was beautiful and held his favor.

sentences.zh: 李仁遇，曦甥也，以色嬖之，用以為相。

translations.literal: Li Renyu was Xi's nephew by his sister; Xi favored him for his looks and made him chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Renyu, Xi's nephew, won favor through his beauty and was made chancellor.

sentences.zh: 曦常為牛飲，群臣侍酒，醉而不勝，有訴及私棄酒者輒殺之。

translations.literal: Xi often held ox drinking-bouts; the ministers attended with wine; those who became drunk beyond endurance, or were reported to have secretly poured away wine, were immediately killed.
translations.idiomatic: Xi often held drinking contests in which ministers had to keep pace. Anyone who became too drunk to continue, or was reported to have secretly discarded wine, was executed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 諸子繼柔棄酒，並殺其贊者一人。

translations.literal: When his son Jirou poured away wine, he also killed one of the attendants who urged him on.
translations.idiomatic: When his son Jirou poured away wine, Xi also executed one of the attendants who had urged him to drink.

sentences.zh: 連重遇殺昶，懼為國人所討，與朱文進連姻以自固。

translations.literal: Lian Chongyu had killed Chang and feared the people of the state would rise against him; he allied his family by marriage with Zhu Wenjin to strengthen himself.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Chongyu, who had killed Chang, feared popular retribution and cemented his position by marrying into Zhu Wenjin's family.

sentences.zh: 曦心疑之，常以語誚重遇等，重遇等流涕自辨。

translations.literal: Xi harbored suspicion in his heart and often mocked Chongyu and the others in speech; Chongyu and the others wept as they defended themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Xi grew suspicious of them and often taunted Chongyu and his allies, who wept as they protested their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 李氏妒尚妃之寵，欲圖曦而立其子亞澄，乃使人謂重遇等曰：「上心不平於二公，奈何？

translations.literal: The Lady Li was jealous of Worthy Consort Shang's favor, wished to plot against Xi and install her son Yacheng, and therefore sent someone to tell Chongyu and the others: "The emperor's heart is ill-disposed toward you two—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li, jealous of Worthy Consort Shang, plotted to overthrow Xi and install her son Yacheng. She sent word to Chongyu and his allies: "The emperor's heart has turned against you—what will you do?

sentences.zh: 」重遇等懼。

translations.literal: " Chongyu and the others were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: " Chongyu and his men were terrified.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，曦出遊，醉歸，重遇等遣壯士拉於馬上而殺之，謚曰景宗。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year Xi went out on an excursion and returned drunk; Chongyu and the others sent stalwart men to drag him onto a horse and kill him; his posthumous title was Sovereign Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixth year Xi went out on an excursion and returned drunk. Chongyu and his allies sent bravos to pull him onto a horse and kill him. He was posthumously titled Sovereign Jing.

sentences.zh: 延政，審知子也。

translations.literal: Yanzheng was Shenzhi's son.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzheng was a son of Shenzhi.

sentences.zh: 曦立，為淫虐，延政數貽書諫之。

translations.literal: When Xi was enthroned and became lewd and cruel, Yanzheng repeatedly sent letters remonstrating with him.
translations.idiomatic: After Xi took the throne and ruled with cruelty and debauchery, Yanzheng repeatedly sent letters of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 曦怒，遣杜建崇監其軍，延政逐之，曦乃舉兵攻延政，為延政所敗。

translations.literal: Xi was angry and sent Du Jianchong to supervise his army; Yanzheng drove him out; Xi then raised troops to attack Yanzheng and was defeated by him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was furious and sent Du Jianchong to supervise Yanzheng's army. Yanzheng expelled him, and when Xi marched against him he was defeated.

sentences.zh: 延政乃以建州建國稱殷，改元天德。

translations.literal: Yanzheng then founded a state at Jian Prefecture, declared himself ruler of Yin, and changed the era name to Heavenly Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzheng then founded the state of Yin at Jianzhou and adopted the era name Heavenly Virtue.

sentences.zh: 是時，南唐李景聞閩亂，發兵攻之，延政遣其從子繼昌守福州，而南唐兵方急攻延政，福州將李仁達謂其徒曰：「唐兵攻建州，富沙王不能自保，其能有此土也？

translations.literal: At that time Li Jing of Southern Tang, hearing of turmoil in Min, sent troops to attack; Yanzheng dispatched his nephew Jichang to hold Fuzhou; while Southern Tang forces were pressing hard against Yanzheng, the Fuzhou general Li Renda said to his followers: "Tang troops are attacking Jian Prefecture; the Prince of Fusha cannot even protect himself—how could he hold this territory?
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing of Southern Tang, hearing of chaos in Min, sent an army to attack. Yanzheng sent his nephew Jichang to hold Fuzhou. While Tang forces pressed Yanzheng hard, Fuzhou general Li Renda told his men, "Tang troops are attacking Jianzhou. The Prince of Fusha cannot even save himself—how can he hold this land?

sentences.zh: 」乃擒繼昌殺之。

translations.literal: " He then seized Jichang and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: " He seized Jichang and killed him.

sentences.zh: 欲自立，懼眾不附，以雪峰寺僧卓儼明示眾曰：「此非常人也。

translations.literal: Wishing to rule himself but fearing the multitude would not follow, he had the Xuefeng Temple monk Zhuo Yanming show himself to the crowd, saying: "This is no ordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to rule himself but fearing the troops would not follow him, he presented the monk Zhuo Yanming of Xuefeng Temple to the crowd, declaring, "This is no ordinary man.

sentences.zh: 」被以袞冕，率諸將吏北面而臣之。

translations.literal: " They clothed him in imperial robes and caps, and the generals and officials led them all to face north and serve him as sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: " They dressed him in imperial robes and led the generals and officials to bow to him as their sovereign.

sentences.zh: 已而又殺儼明，乃自立，送款於李景，景以仁達為威武軍節度使，更其名曰弘義。

translations.literal: Before long he killed Yanming as well and ruled himself; he sent submission to Li Jing; Jing appointed Renda military governor of the Weiwu Army and changed his name to Hongyi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he killed Yanming as well and ruled in his own name. He submitted to Li Jing, who appointed him military governor of the Weiwu Army and changed his name to Hongyi.

sentences.zh: 而景兵攻破建州，遷延政族於金陵，封鄱陽王。

translations.literal: Jing's troops then captured Jian Prefecture, moved Yanzheng's clan to Jinling, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tang forces then captured Jianzhou, moved Yanzheng's clan to Jinling, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 是歲，景保大四年也。

translations.literal: That year was the fourth year of Baoda of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: This occurred in the fourth year of Jing's Baoda era.

sentences.zh: 留從效聞延政降唐，執王繼勛送於金陵，李景以泉州為清源軍，以從效為節度使。

translations.literal: Liu Congxiao, hearing that Yanzheng had submitted to Tang, seized Wang Jixun and sent him to Jinling; Li Jing made Quanzhou the Qingyuan Army district and appointed Congxiao its military governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Congxiao learned Yanzheng had surrendered to Tang, he seized Wang Jixun and sent him to Jinling. Li Jing organized Quanzhou as the Qingyuan military circuit and appointed Congxiao its governor.

sentences.zh: 景已破延政，遣人召李仁達入朝，仁達不從，遂降於吳越。

translations.literal: Jing had already defeated Yanzheng and sent someone to summon Li Renda to court; Renda would not obey and therefore submitted to Wuyue.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Yanzheng, Jing summoned Li Renda to court. Renda refused and submitted to Wuyue instead.

sentences.zh: 而留從效亦逐景守兵，據泉、漳二州，景猶封從效晉江王。

translations.literal: Liu Congxiao also drove out Jing's garrison troops and held the two prefectures of Quan and Zhang; Jing still enfeoffed Congxiao as Prince of Jinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congxiao also expelled Tang garrisons and held Quanzhou and Zhangzhou. Jing still enfeoffed him as Prince of Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 周世宗時，從效遣牙將蔡仲興為商人，間道至京師，求置邸內屬。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Shizong of Zhou, Congxiao sent the牙 general Cai Zhongxing disguised as a merchant by a secret route to the capital to request establishment of a lodge and inclusion within the empire.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Shizong of Zhou, Congxiao sent general Cai Zhongxing disguised as a merchant along a secret route to the capital to request a diplomatic lodge and recognition as a Zhou dependency.

sentences.zh: 是時，世宗與李景畫江為界，遂不納，從效仍臣於南唐。

translations.literal: At that time Shizong and Li Jing had drawn the Yangtze as a boundary, so he did not accept them; Congxiao still submitted to Southern Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong had just drawn the Yangtze as his boundary with Li Jing and declined the request. Congxiao remained a vassal of Southern Tang.

sentences.zh: 其後事具國史。

translations.literal: Subsequent events are fully recorded in the dynastic histories.
translations.idiomatic: Later events are recorded in full in the dynastic histories.
